articles.title: Secret Whale Tracker: How Undersea Internet Cables Can Spy on Silent Giants
articles.summary: Whales are super quiet most of the time, so how do we track them? Scientists just found a way to use the internet cables on the ocean floor to feel the water ripples whales make when they swim. This could help protect whales as the ocean changes.

articles.title: Why Do Chatbots Always Say '7'? The Secret Groupthink Problem in AI
articles.summary: Ask a chatbot for a random number between 1 and 10, and it almost always says 7. That's because AI models are stuck in a rut—they give the same boring answers to lots of questions. A new startup called Springboards built a model that's way more creative.

articles.title: Wasted Wind Power Could Make Green Hydrogen Way Cheaper
articles.summary: Sometimes wind and solar farms make too much electricity and it goes to waste. Scientists in Germany found a clever use for it: making clean hydrogen fuel. By using this extra power, hydrogen could become almost €2 cheaper per kilogram.
